- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model tends to overshoot and continue upward; apply a downward correction of 3–8% in the next 5–7 days if sentiment is mixed or slightly negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative signals (e.g., >3 negative values in 10 days), model should adjust downward by 5–10% in the next 10-day horizon.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts; if model shows >10% upward trend from 10-day average, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is positive but price drops sharply (e.g., >5% in 3 days), model should not assume continuation; apply a 2–5% downward bias for next 5 days.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike (e.g., >10% from peak), model should reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 3–5 days, regardless of sentiment.
- Model underestimates price drops in the final 5–7 days of forecast horizon; add 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
